messages.content: I would like the average price of bitcoin at the end of each business week in 2023

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

The user wants the average price of Bitcoin at the end of each business week in 2023. They likely want a list of dates (end of each business week) and the average price on that day. We need to fetch Bitcoin price data. We can use an API like CoinGecko or CoinAPI. But we have only the Open-Meteo API tool, which is for weather. That doesn't help. We need to get Bitcoin price data. We don't have a tool for that. We could use a public API like CoinGecko's simple price endpoint. But we don't have a tool to call arbitrary URLs? We only have the requests_get function for Open-Meteo. But maybe we can use it to call other APIs? The function is generic: it takes a URL, headers, params. So we can use it to call CoinGecko API. The function is named requests_get, but it's generic. So we can call e.g., https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/bitcoin/market_chart?vs_currency=usd&days=365&interval=daily. That returns daily prices. Then we can compute average price at the end of each business week. Business week ends on Friday. So we need to get price for each Friday in 2023. We need to consider business week: Monday to Friday. So end of each business week is Friday. So we need price on each Friday in 2023. We need average price at the end of each business week: maybe average of that day's price? Or average of the week? The phrase "average price of bitcoin at the end of each business week" could mean the average price on that day (closing price). But "average price" might refer to average of the week? But "at the end of each business week" suggests the price at the end of the week. So maybe they want the closing price on each Friday. But they say "average price". Could be the average of the week? But "at the end" implies a single point. So maybe they want the average price of the week, but at the end of the week? That is ambiguous. I'd interpret as the average price of Bitcoin for each week, reported at the end of the week. So we need to compute weekly average price for each week in 2023. That means for each week (Monday to Friday), compute average of daily closing prices, then report that average on the Friday. So we need daily price data for 2023. We can fetch daily prices via CoinGecko. Let's do that.

We need to call the API: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/bitcoin/market_chart?vs_currency=usd&days=365&interval=daily. But that returns data for the last 365 days from now. We need 2023 specifically. We can use the "from" and "to" parameters: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/bitcoin/market_chart/range?vs_currency=usd&from=timestamp&to=timestamp. So we can set from Jan 1 2023 to Dec 31 2023. Timestamps in seconds. Jan 1 2023 00:00 UTC is 1672531200. Dec 31 2023 23:59 UTC is 1704067199. So we can call that. The response includes "prices" array of [timestamp, price]. We can parse that.

We need to use the requests_get function. Provide URL, params. Let's do that.
